svg.title: Cross-Chain Messaging: Commit, Relay, Verify, Execute
svg.desc: A source application creates a message through a source endpoint and records a message commitment. A relayer transports the payload with a proof or attestation to the destination chain. The destination verifier checks the evidence and message domain, replay protection marks the message as consumed, and the receiving application executes the authorized action. An authenticated acknowledgement or proven timeout can complete the packet lifecycle. Transport and authentication are separate security jobs.
svg.text: CROSS-CHAIN MESSAGING
A message is transported, authenticated, and executed across separate state machines
RELAY ≠ VERIFY
1 · Source chain application
Authorize payload and call the source messaging endpoint.
Destination chain application
Only acts after the destination verification and policy checks.
2 · Source commitment / event
Unique message ID + source/destination domain + payload hash
Source-chain state binds the message to its origin and content.
3 · Relayer / transport network
Observe source finality, obtain payload and proof/attestation,
then pay destination gas and submit a relay transaction.
4 · Destination verifier
Check light-client proof, commitment, threshold attestation,
or the configured verification mechanism.
Security depends on the verifier's trust model and source finality.
5 · Destination domain + replay protection
Validate origin, recipient, nonce/sequence, and payload.
Atomically mark the message consumed before privileged effects.
Reject duplicates, wrong-chain replays, and unauthorized senders.
6 · Destination execution
Run the receiving application handler or contract callback.
Authenticated origin does not make every payload safe.
7 · Acknowledgement / status
Where supported, record the destination result and prove it
back to the source; status semantics are protocol-specific.
Timeout and recovery (where supported)
A proven timeout may unlock source-side recovery; it must exclude late execution.
Review: source finality · verifier model · destination domain · replay state · acknowledgements/timeouts · upgrade authority
Messaging is a primitive; a token bridge adds asset accounting, mint/burn/lock/release and withdrawal rules.
